name: São Miguel, Azores
summary: One volcanic island. Crater lakes, hot springs, tea fields, and a whale watch with a spare day in case the sea says no. Quiet, green, and a long way from both home airports.
why: April is mild rather than hot, the island is never a capital-city trip, and the wildlife is the educational event. Two bases are enough for two weeks. You do not need a second island.
distinctive: A green crater you can drive around, fumaroles in a town garden, and sperm whales that live offshore all year.
weather: A São Miguel climate guide puts a typical April near 18°C by day, 13°C at night, with roughly 80 mm of rain and a sea around 16°C. Cloud on the crater rims can sit there while the coast is clear. Waterproof layers are the packing list.
crowds: April is outside European summer. The island has busy viewpoints on clear afternoons and is otherwise quiet by mainland-Europe standards. Whale boats have a passenger limit, which is the crowd control.
natureExperiences: Sete Cidades and the twin lakes, on a clear window
Furnas, the lake, and the steaming ground in Terra Nostra
A whale-and-dolphin watch from Ponta Delgada or Vila Franca do Campo
age6: Lake shores, a garden with a warm pool, a tea factory, and a boat only if the sea is kind and the operator takes small children.
age12: The whale briefing, the crater viewpoints, and the hot-spring science.
age14: The same, plus the old whaling lookouts and why the hunt stopped. Faial's university boats are the deeper version, and they require a second island this plan does not take.
adults: Slow driving, cooking in a volcanic valley, and a landscape that changes with each ridge. Nightlife is not the product.
gettingAround: A car, or two. Roads are narrow, green and sometimes cow-paced. Portugal drives on the right. Do not add Terceira or Pico unless you are willing to lose a day to weather. Inter-island flights cancel.
meetingPoint: Ponta Delgada, almost always via Lisbon or another European hub. From Melbourne this is one of the longest journeys in the set. From India it is also a two- or three-flight day. The island is the reward after a hard journey, which is why it ranks lower on practicality.
visaAu: Same Schengen position as mainland Portugal. Australian passports are visa-free for a short stay, EES biometrics apply at the first Schengen entry, and ETIAS was not yet operating.
visaIn: Indian passports need a Schengen visa. If the whole trip is the Azores, Portugal is the country to apply to. The islands are not a separate visa.
disadvantages: The flight from Melbourne is the weakest logistics in the shortlist.
Rain and hill cloud will hide at least one famous view. The spare days are the plan, not a failure.
The sea is about 16°C. Swimming with dolphins is a separate, colder, rule-bound choice. Watching from the boat is the family default.
Two weeks on one island is quiet on purpose. If the 14-year-old needs cities, this is the wrong first choice.
uncertainties: Whale sightings. Visit Portugal says sperm whales and dolphins are a year-round possibility and that blue whales are often seen in spring between São Miguel and Santa Maria. Nothing is guaranteed, and boats cancel in rough seas.
2027 flights via Lisbon for seven people.
Which Terra Nostra pool rules apply to children that season.

image.credit: Wikimedia Commons: Lagoa das Sete Cidades

gain: The quietest dramatic nature, with a real chance of whales and almost no famous-city noise.
miss: A sane flight from Melbourne, and the culture and history depth of Japan or Türkiye.
stretch16: Add two weather-buffer days, not a second island.

days.experience: Land and walk the waterfront. Stop.
days.optional: The city gates and one pineapple greenhouse if it is two minutes away
days.highlight: A small harbour capital in black-and-white stone
days.kids: Gelato and an early night after the long flight.
days.transfer: Via Lisbon or another hub. Door to door from Melbourne can take well over 30 hours. From India, plan on two flights at least.
days.seasonal: April rain can start the moment you land. That is normal.
days.wet: The hotel. Do not drive to a viewpoint in the dark.

days.experience: Sete Cidades when the rim is clear. If it is not, swap with a later day.
days.optional: A short shore walk at the green lake, not a full crater hike
days.highlight: Two lakes in a volcanic bowl, one greener and one bluer
days.kids: Viewpoints and a lakeside half hour. The rim road is the activity.
days.seasonal: Cloud on the rim is the classic disappointment. Keep this day movable.
days.wet: Gorreana tea or the city pineapple houses, and try the lakes tomorrow.

days.experience: Whale watch, booked with a spare day later in the week.
days.optional: The whale museum or a lookout if the boat cancels
days.highlight: Sperm whales or dolphins, if the sea allows
days.kids: Ask the operator about age and sea-sickness before you pay. A 6-year-old on a rough day is a miserable scientist.
days.transfer: Boats leave from Ponta Delgada and Vila Franca do Campo. Half a day is realistic.
days.seasonal: Visit Portugal notes spring blue whales in the channel toward Santa Maria, and year-round operators on São Miguel. Sightings are never owed to you.
days.wet: A rough sea is a cancel, not a dare. Use the museum.

days.experience: Gorreana tea fields and a black-sand or rock coast viewpoint.
days.optional: A second crater, Lagoa do Fogo, only if the road is clear
days.highlight: Europe's oldest tea plantation still picking on this island
days.kids: The factory tour is short and smells like tea. The coast walk stays behind the walls.
days.transfer: Under an hour to the north coast.
days.seasonal: North-coast waves are for looking. Swimming is not the April plan.

days.experience: Move to Furnas. Terra Nostra garden and the warm pool.
days.optional: The steaming fumaroles by the lake, from the path
days.highlight: A valley that cooks and grows at the same time
days.kids: The warm earth and the garden pool are the 6-year-old's best hour on the island. Check pool rules and temperature.
days.transfer: About an hour from Ponta Delgada.
days.seasonal: The cozido stew cooked in the ground is a fun sight and a heavy meal. Order one to share.
days.wet: The garden is the point of a wet day. Take a change of clothes for the pool.

days.experience: Furnas Lake and a short forest walk.
days.highlight: A crater lake with fumaroles on the shore
days.kids: Stay on the built paths near the steam. It is not a climbing day.
days.seasonal: Sulphur smells. Some children hate it and then get used to it.
days.wet: The botanical garden again. There is enough there for two visits.

days.experience: A free day, or the spare whale watch if the first boat cancelled.
days.highlight: The buffer that makes a nature island work
days.transfer: Back to Ponta Delgada only if a boat is booked. About an hour.
days.seasonal: This is the day you move to when Sete Cidades was in cloud.

days.experience: Nordeste or a waterfall on the east coast, and back.
days.optional: A short end of the road and a picnic
days.highlight: The greener, emptier end of the island
days.kids: Viewpoints. Do not commit to a long muddy trail.
days.transfer: Allow a couple of hours of driving in total, plus stops.
days.seasonal: Narrow roads. Two confident drivers if you take both cars.
days.wet: Cancel the east and keep the garden.

days.experience: Return to the city for the last nights, nearer the airport.
days.optional: A fort and a swim in a hotel pool, not the sea
days.seasonal: Use a clear evening for any viewpoint you missed.
days.wet: The car is still useful. Do not stand on a rim in a gale.

days.experience: The spare whale day, or a pineapples-and-town day if you already saw whales.
days.highlight: A second chance at the animals, which is the only serious way to plan it
days.kids: If the first boat was rough, do not force a second on the 6-year-old.
days.seasonal: Spring is a strong month for variety of species. It is still the ocean.

days.optional: The Carlos Machado natural history museum for the 12- and 14-year-olds
days.kids: An hour, not a morning of glass cases, unless they are absorbed.

days.experience: One last clear-weather viewpoint you missed. Otherwise nothing.
days.optional: Sete Cidades at a different hour of day
days.highlight: Leaving a place you now know how to drive
days.seasonal: If every rim day was cloudy, this is the last throw. If not, rest.

days.experience: Buffer day before the long flight.
days.seasonal: Atlantic wind delays happen. Do not fly to Lisbon on the same day as an onward intercontinental flight if you can avoid it.

days.highlight: A long journey home, already priced into the decision
days.transfer: Ponta Delgada to Lisbon is often about 2.5 hours, then a separate long haul. Confirm the connection time for seven people and a missed-wave plan.
days.seasonal: This is why the Azores loses to New Zealand on practicality for a Melbourne family.
